name: COEUR MINING, INC.
moat_justification: Pure price-taker on gold/silver with zero pricing power; what passes for a moat in mining is cost-curve position and reserve quality. Las Chispas is a genuinely high-grade, low-cost asset and the seven-mine portfolio is diversified across the U.S., Mexico and Canada, but reserves deplete, the acquired Canadian mines are still ramping, and growth has been bought with dilutive all-stock deals.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 30.7%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.3x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Price-taking precious-metals miner, moat 3/10 — TTM OE inflected on the SilverCrest and New Gold deals plus high metal prices, but at $15.55 the weighted IRR is only 11.0% (IV@15 $10.56); it clears 15% only below ~$10.56.
moat_for: Las Chispas: high-grade, low-cost silver-gold mine (real cost-curve asset)
Seven-mine diversification across U.S., Mexico and Canada
Leading silver-producer scale post-New Gold, plus copper from New Afton
Net-cash balance sheet; record FCF funds exploration and buybacks
moat_against: Zero pricing power — revenue is the gold/silver spot price
Reserves deplete yearly; replacement needs capex or dilutive M&A
New Afton/Rainy River still ramping; 2026 guidance trimmed in Q2
Cost inflation and Mexico permitting/jurisdiction exposure
